papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Towards Imperceptible and Robust Adversarial Example Attacks against Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Machine learning systems based on deep neural networks, being able to produce state-of-the-art results on various perception tasks, have gained mainstream adoption in many applications. However, they are shown to be vulnerable to adversarial example attack, which generates malicious output by adding slight perturbations to the input. Previous adversarial example crafting methods, however, use simple metrics to evaluate the distances between the original examples and the adversarial ones, which could be easily detected by human eyes. In addition, these attacks are often not robust due to the inevitable noises and deviation in the physical world. In this work, we present a new adversarial example attack crafting method, which takes the human perceptual system into consideration and maximizes the noise tolerance of the crafted adversarial example. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed technique.

papers.title: Robust Real-World Image Super-Resolution against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: Recently deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved significant success in real-world image super-resolution (SR). However, adversarial image samples with quasi-imperceptible noises could threaten deep learning SR models. In this paper, we propose a robust deep learning framework for real-world SR that randomly erases potential adversarial noises in the frequency domain of input images or features. The rationale is that on the SR task clean images or features have a different pattern from the attacked ones in the frequency domain. Observing that existing adversarial attacks usually add high-frequency noises to input images, we introduce a novel random frequency mask module that blocks out high-frequency components possibly containing the harmful perturbations in a stochastic manner. Since the frequency masking may not only destroys the adversarial perturbations but also affects the sharp details in a clean image, we further develop an adversarial sample classifier based on the frequency domain of images to determine if applying the proposed mask module. Based on the above ideas, we devise a novel real-world image SR framework that combines the proposed frequency mask modules and the proposed adversarial classifier with an existing super-resolution backbone network. Experiments show that our proposed method is more insensitive to adversarial attacks and presents more stable SR results than existing models and defenses.

literature_themes.theme: Defense Mechanisms Against Data Poisoning Attacks in AI Models
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers primarily investigates the vulnerabilities of AI models, particularly in recommendation systems and computer vision, to data poisoning attacks. It explores various defense mechanisms, including novel detection algorithms, robust optimization strategies, and dual-defense frameworks that combine active and passive defenses. The studies highlight the significant impact of data poisoning on model performance and propose methods to enhance resilience and detection accuracy across different applications.
literature_themes.limitations: The cluster lacks comprehensive abstracts for all papers, limiting the understanding of the third paper's contributions. Additionally, while various defense mechanisms are proposed, the effectiveness of these methods in real-world scenarios and their scalability across diverse datasets remain underexplored.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster can support research gap identification by highlighting the need for more robust, scalable, and practical defense mechanisms against data poisoning attacks, particularly in real-world applications. It also emphasizes the importance of integrating advanced detection techniques, such as GANs, into existing frameworks to improve model integrity.

literature_themes.theme: Adversarial Robustness in Deep Learning Applications
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on enhancing the robustness of deep learning models against adversarial attacks, particularly in the contexts of adversarial example crafting and image super-resolution. The first paper introduces a method that considers human perception to create less detectable adversarial examples, while the second paper proposes a framework that utilizes frequency domain analysis to mitigate the impact of adversarial noise in image super-resolution tasks.
literature_themes.limitations: Both studies acknowledge the challenge of ensuring that the proposed methods do not compromise the integrity of clean images or the performance of the models. Additionally, the effectiveness of these techniques in diverse real-world scenarios remains to be fully validated.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the need for further research into the intersection of human perceptual systems and adversarial robustness, as well as the exploration of frequency domain techniques in various deep learning applications, thus identifying potential gaps in existing literature on adversarial defenses.

summary: The literature reveals significant vulnerabilities of AI systems to data poisoning and adversarial attacks, with proposed defense mechanisms including dual-defense frameworks and frequency domain analysis. However, the effectiveness of these defenses in diverse real-world applications remains underexplored, highlighting a critical gap for robust, scalable solutions. Future research should focus on integrating advanced detection techniques and validating proposed methods across various AI domains to enhance model resilience.
literature_tension_graph: The literature presents a tension between the effectiveness of proposed dual-defense frameworks against data poisoning attacks in recommendation systems (P2) and the limited validation of these frameworks across diverse AI applications (P1). While P2 demonstrates improved resilience, it remains confined to a specific domain, raising questions about the generalizability of such defenses. Additionally, the adversarial robustness methods focusing on human perception (P4) do not address the need for robust defenses against newly crafted adversarial examples, indicating a gap in the evaluation of defense mechanisms across different attack types. This unresolved condition suggests a research direction that integrates dual-defense strategies with frequency domain techniques to enhance robustness against both data poisoning and adversarial attacks in a broader range of AI systems.
scholarly_positioning: Prior research has extensively documented the vulnerabilities of AI systems to data poisoning and adversarial attacks, proposing various defense mechanisms such as dual-defense frameworks and frequency domain analysis. However, these approaches often lack validation across diverse real-world applications, leaving a significant gap in their practical applicability and scalability. Existing studies primarily focus on specific domains, such as recommendation systems and image super-resolution, without addressing the broader implications for AI resilience. This proposed research aims to develop a comprehensive framework that integrates advanced detection techniques and robust defenses, thereby situating itself within the ongoing discourse on enhancing the integrity and reliability of AI systems against evolving threats.
domain_router: machine-learning method development; The proposed methodology should involve ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of integrated detection techniques and defense mechanisms across diverse AI applications.
research_scope: This study will focus on enhancing the robustness of deep learning models in image classification tasks against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The target population will include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on benchmark datasets such as CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. The proposed intervention will involve a dual-defense framework that integrates advanced detection techniques, including GAN-based anomaly detection and frequency domain analysis, evaluated over a 6-month period. The control group will consist of traditional defense mechanisms currently used in the literature. Primary outcomes will measure classification accuracy and resilience to attacks, while secondary outcomes will assess the computational efficiency and scalability of the proposed framework across various datasets.
concept_definition:
{
  "Robust AI Systems": "AI systems designed to maintain performance and reliability despite adversarial conditions, such as data poisoning and adversarial attacks.",
  "Data Poisoning": "A type of attack where maliciously altered training data is introduced to degrade the performance of machine learning models.",
  "Adversarial Attacks": "Techniques that involve manipulating input data to deceive AI models into making incorrect predictions or classifications.",
  "Deep Learning Models": "Neural network architectures, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), used for processing and classifying visual data.",
  "Image Classification Tasks": "The process of categorizing images into predefined classes based on their content.",
  "Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)": "A class of deep learning models specifically designed for processing structured grid data like images, utilizing convolutional layers to extract features.",
  "Benchmark Datasets": "Standardized datasets, such as CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, used for evaluating the performance of machine learning models.",
  "Dual-Defense Framework": "An integrated approach combining multiple defense mechanisms to enhance the resilience of AI systems against attacks.",
  "GAN-based Anomaly Detection": "A technique utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to identify unusual patterns in data that may indicate a poisoning attack.",
  "Frequency Domain Analysis": "A method of analyzing signals or data in the frequency domain to detect anomalies or alterations that may signify attacks.",
  "Ablation Studies": "Experimental studies that systematically remove or alter components of a model to assess their impact on performance and validate the effectiveness of proposed techniques.",
  "Classification Accuracy": "The ratio of correctly predicted instances to the total instances in a dataset, measuring the performance of a classification model.",
  "Resilience to Attacks": "The ability of a model to maintain its performance despite attempts to compromise it through adversarial methods.",
  "Computational Efficiency": "The measure of the resources (time, memory) required by a model to perform its tasks, indicating its operational viability.",
  "Scalability": "The capability of a defense mechanism to maintain performance when applied to larger datasets or more complex scenarios.",
  "Research Gap": "The identified lack of studies addressing the generalizability and effectiveness of dual-defense frameworks across various AI applications, particularly in image classification."
}
technical_feasibility: The study requires access to open-source deep learning models (CNNs) for experimentation, labeled benchmark datasets (CIFAR-10, ImageNet) for training and evaluation, and GPU resources for computational efficiency. It does not require hidden state extraction, multilingual prompt sets, or human participants, as it focuses on model performance metrics. Since the study does not involve user trust, no human-subject design is necessary. The design is feasible as long as the required resources are available; however, if only API models are accessible, the methodology should be adjusted to focus on output-level evaluations rather than internal representation analysis.

The mediator in this causal chain is the enhanced detection capability of adversarial inputs, which is expected to improve the resilience of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, leading to the dependent variable of classification accuracy. proposal: This research addresses the critical gap in the generalizability of dual-defense frameworks against data poisoning and adversarial attacks in AI systems, particularly within image classification tasks. Prior studies, such as those focusing on recommendation systems, have demonstrated the effectiveness of dual-defense mechanisms; however, they lack validation across diverse AI applications, leaving unresolved tensions regarding their scalability and robustness in real-world scenarios. This study proposes a novel theoretical framework that integrates GAN-based anomaly detection with frequency domain analysis, enhancing the detection capabilities of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) against adversarial inputs. The hypothesis posits that this integration will yield significantly higher classification accuracy compared to traditional defense mechanisms, mediated by improved detection of adversarial examples. Methodologically, the research will employ comprehensive ablation studies utilizing benchmark datasets (CIFAR-10 and ImageNet) to rigorously evaluate the proposed framework against established control groups. Key operational definitions will clarify constructs such as 'robust AI systems' and 'adversarial attacks,' ensuring precise measurement of outcomes like classification accuracy and resilience to attacks. This proposal not only advances theoretical understanding by elucidating the mechanisms behind dual-defense strategies but also provides actionable insights for deploying robust AI systems in practical applications, thereby addressing the limitations of existing literature and enhancing the operational viability of AI technologies.
